market_summary: Friday's US close was a broad tech sell-off: S&P 500 -1.1% to 7,659.44, Nasdaq -2.1% to 26,140.03 and Dow -0.3% to 52,002.41; for the week the Nasdaq lost 4.5% (worst week since June), the S&P 500 1.9% and the Russell 2000 3.0%, while the Dow gained 0.7%. The Philadelphia semiconductor index fell 3.83% to 11,137.29, an eighth straight loss and the longest streak since 2008; it is down 15.7% from Oct 6 and 23.9% below its June record (Nvidia -10.5% and Micron -15.9% since Oct 6, TSMC's ADR -2.3% Friday), with AI-financing worries, China memory competition and oil cited. Rates did not drive it: the 10-year sat near 5.09-5.11%, down from 5.27% on Oct 6, and October hike odds fell to about 15-16% (from about a third Thursday) after Warsh gave no signal, while futures still lean to a December hike (about 74% on CME FedWatch per AP; one money-market read about 89%); Friday data were firm, with September import prices +1.1% (fuel +4.8%) and industrial production +0.7% (0.4% expected). Brent touched $110 for the first time since May and settled at $109.86 (+3.7%, about +5% on the week) and WTI at $101.41 (+3.5%, over +10% on the week) as Iran stepped up Hormuz attacks and the Houthis fired on Saudi Arabia; the UK monitor counted 10 Hormuz attacks this week and a tanker was hit off Saudi Arabia on Friday. Gold was about $4,165-4,180, bitcoin about $81,500, the VIX near 20; in Hong Kong on Friday the Hang Seng closed +0.52% at 24,186.83 and HS Tech +1.16% at 4,108.24. The FOMC blackout started today, so no Fed speakers before the decision. Next: China Q3 GDP (4.4% y/y expected), retail sales and industrial output 13:00 AEDT Mon Oct 19; Netflix 07:01 AEDT Wed Oct 21; SAP 07:05, Meta and TI 07:30, IBM and Lam 08:00, Tesla 08:30 AEDT Thu Oct 22; US leading index 01:00 AEDT Fri Oct 23; Spotify Q&A 23:00 AEDT Thu Oct 22; US flash PMIs 00:45 and UMich final 01:00 AEDT Sat Oct 24; AU CPI 11:30 AEDT Wed Oct 28; Fed decision 05:00 AEDT Thu Oct 29.

AMZN.reason: Down 1.9% Friday and 4.7% for the week as the Nasdaq fell 2.1% on doubts over AI-infrastructure payback and tech borrowing. No company news found for Oct 16-17. Q3 about Fri Oct 30 07:00 AEDT. Hold.

AXOS.reason: Up 0.7% Friday and down only 0.3% for the week, the steadiest holding. The 10-year yield held near 5.09% while stocks fell, and October hike odds eased to about 17%. Fiscal Q1 Fri Oct 30 08:00 AEDT. Hold.

BABA.reason: US ADR fell 1.8% Friday (-2.0% week) with the US tech selloff, after Hong Kong shares rose 2.3% earlier Friday as the Hang Seng Tech index gained 1.2%. The Qwen-powered Apple Intelligence beta is still due in China later in October. China Q3 GDP Mon Oct 19 13:00 AEDT. Hold.

ENPH.reason: Down 0.6% Friday and 6.7% for the week, a choppy run that included -8.4% Wednesday and +5.0% Thursday. No company news found. Q3 call Wed Oct 28 07:30 AEDT. Watch.

FIGR.reason: Down 2.0% Friday after Thursday's 10.5% jump, leaving it 4.9% lower for the week. Mortgage News Daily's 30-year ticked up 0.04 points to 7.37% Friday but is still 0.27 points below Oct 7. No company news found; still near its 52-week low, so the watch flag stays live. Hold.

GOOGL.reason: Down 2.5% Friday and 3.1% for the week as AI-linked names sold off on spending and debt worries. Nothing company-specific changed, and TSMC's raised 2026 outlook (about 44% growth, AI demand above supply) still supports the TPU and Cloud case. Q3 results 07:30 AEDT Thu Oct 29. Add stays.

LDI.reason: Down 5.8% Friday, giving back much of Thursday's 14.4% jump, and 5.0% lower for the week. Mortgage News Daily's 30-year rose 0.04 points to 7.37% Friday, and the stock remains under the NYSE minimum-price standard. Trim.

META.reason: Down 3.7% Friday and 1.3% for the week as AI spenders sold off and CoreWeave, a major Meta compute supplier, fell more than 11% on credit fears. No company news found. Q3 call Thu Oct 22 07:30 AEDT, where capex guidance is the test. Hold.

MRVL.reason: Down 5.6% Friday and 17.2% for the week, the worst holding, as chip stocks fell on doubts that AI-infrastructure spending will pay off. No company news found; TSMC's call still points to custom-chip demand above supply. Hold, but this is now the biggest weekly drawdown in the book.

MU.reason: Down 5.6% Friday and 14.6% for the week as CXMT DRAM fears and AI-spending doubts hit memory again. Micron's COO said the new Taichung plant's 2027 capacity is sold out, and Taiwan's president urged both sides to negotiate. Union rally in Taipei Mon Oct 19; Taichung mediation Thu Oct 22. Watch.

NFLX.reason: Down 2.9% Friday but up 0.3% for the week, the only holding higher. Netflix named former Disney TV chair Peter Rice chief content officer from Oct 26, replacing Bela Bajaria, a day after confirming 6% job cuts. Q3 results Wed Oct 21 07:00 AEDT. Hold into the print.

NVDA.reason: Down 1.4% Friday and 6.6% for the week. CoreWeave fell more than 11% Friday with swaps pricing more than a 50% chance of default within five years, a day after Huang said it needed no backstop. GTC Berlin Oct 20-22. Hold.

RKT.reason: Down 2.6% Friday and 6.1% for the week. Mortgage News Daily's 30-year rose 0.04 points to 7.37% Friday, though it is 0.27 points lower than Oct 7, a gain MND ties to AI-selloff fears rather than softer inflation. Q3 around Oct 29. Watch.

TSM.reason: ADR down 2.3% Friday and 9.0% for the week despite a record quarter, a 2026 growth outlook raised to about 44% and Q4 guidance above consensus. The selloff is about AI-spending sentiment, not TSMC's numbers. Add stays.

STRIPE.reason: No new round, tender or secondary mark found; the last tender was February at $159 billion, so the mark multiple stays 2.27. No company news found for Oct 16-17. Hold.

OPENAI.reason: No close found for the roughly $30 billion round at about $1.4 trillion pre-money, so the mark multiple stays 5.43. Reuters reports Anthropic investors now discuss a lower IPO valuation (about $1.5 trillion, down from about $2 trillion) after its Q3 growth slowed, a softer read-across for AI-lab marks. Hold.

headlines: Nasdaq fell 2.1% Friday, its worst week since June (-4.5%); chip index down eight straight days, 24% off its June high.
Rough week for AI holdings: Marvell -17%, Micron -15%, TSMC ADR -9%, Nvidia -7%; Netflix the only holding up.
CoreWeave fell 11% Friday, about 25% on the week, as its 2031 bond yield topped 16%; neocloud bellwether stays bearish.
Reuters: some Anthropic investors now discuss a $1.5T IPO valuation, down from about $2T, after Q3 growth slowed to 45%.
Brent touched $110 on Hormuz and Saudi attacks; October Fed hike odds fell to about 15-17% after Warsh gave no signal.
Next: China Q3 GDP Mon 13:00 AEDT (4.4% expected); Netflix Wed 07:00 AEDT; Meta Thu 07:30 AEDT; Tesla Thu 08:30 AEDT.
